resources.string: Privacy
What this can look like — and what it isn’t

Analytics can suggest a rough sketch (rough place, device, podcast taste) — never a precise profile, and never age or gender. Analytics never includes your name or email. An account is optional and only backs up and syncs your library; it’s never linked to your analytics.
The only personal details that show up are ones you type into search or AI chat. Please don’t.
And again: never sold, never for ads. boxlore will never have ads.
1 · App use
Screen opens, feature taps, settings changes, and rough time spent. Things like home carousel swipes, explore searches, library visits, settings opens, mini-player taps — and a few more of that kind.

So we can see how many people are actually using boxlore, which parts feel alive, and which ones flop — so we can make better product calls. And honestly, so we can watch the charts and feel happy that people are using something we built.
Earlier builds had a Radio feature. Usage showed almost nobody used it, so we removed it instead of keeping dead weight in the app.
2 · Search and onboarding text
Search queries and what the app returns, plus AI onboarding chat text. AI onboarding runs on Groq using %1$s.

Podcast Index and Apple’s APIs lean hard on exact-word matching. Search quality is one of the biggest pain points we’re trying to fix, so seeing real queries and responses is critical. Same for AI onboarding — we need to know whether prompts are understood and answers stay relevant.

A lot of people typed real podcast names and treated the AI like a search box. The model kept asking generic taste questions instead of helping. So we added a layer that checks if the text is basically a show name, validates it against the chat context, and offers “use search instead” with that title so you can subscribe — while the AI still uses it as a taste baseline and the chat continues.
3 · Listening activity
Podcast and episode details, playback progress, likes, subscriptions, downloads, and related listening signals.

Podcast Index charts aren’t great for this, and Apple charts don’t really give us the play-level signal we need. We use this to understand listening activity, and to build community charts that are native to boxlore.
4 · App and device

App version, OS, device details, local hour and day, your analytics ID, and approximate location (country, region, city and postcode area) that PostHog works out from your IP address. The IP address itself isn’t kept.

Most of this PostHog collects by default, and we don’t currently have a clean way to turn that part off. We do use rough location to see which countries boxlore is used in — for example, to check that support prices make sense in each country once payments are on. boxlore never asks for or reads your phone’s location.
5 · Crashes
Technical errors and crash reports.
Pretty obvious — if the app breaks, we need to know so we can fix it.
6 · Support page test
Which of six Support boxlore designs you see, which support levels you look at, whether you tap to pay, and how long you stay on that page.

This is part design survey, part our attempt to earn back what it costs to keep boxlore running. We just want a rough idea of which designs lead more people to support boxlore. It’s tied only to your anonymous analytics ID, never your name, email or account.
7 · Feedback

What you write when you send feedback, the type you pick, and the app version. If you leave “Include device diagnostics” on: your phone model, Android version, network type, audio output and language, plus boxlore’s own recent logs with keys, sign-in details and email addresses removed. Any photos or screenshots you attach.

So the boxlore team can read it, reply, and fix what broke. Your conversations are kept on our servers and tied to this phone (and to your account if you’re signed in), not to your analytics ID. The team reads and answers in Telegram, which gets your message, its type, your phone model, app version and photos — never your email, logs or analytics ID. Photos are deleted 60 days after a conversation is solved or closed. To delete your conversations, email privacy@aswin.cx.
On-device recommendations
Your learned taste profile and ranking model stay on this device. They are not uploaded. JSON backups you create include this state so an imported install can continue with the same learning.

Our promise
From the people building boxlore
boxlore isn’t meant for monetary gain. It’s a few friends finishing a childhood dream — watching code turn into magic on screens.
What that means for your data
Never sold
Never for ads
No ads in boxlore
Usage only

Whatever we collect will never be sold, never used to push ads, and never used for the other creepy things people do with data. It’s only to understand how many people use the app, how they use it, and which features work or don’t.
